chunks: And in the narration of al-Sakuni:

That ʿAlī عليه السلام was brought a man who had incurred a hadd punishment, and he had many sores on his body. So ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “Leave him until he recovers; do not irritate them against him and thereby kill him.”

key_terms.أَقِرُّوهُ: leave him and do not proceed against him immediately
key_terms.حَتَّى يَبْرَأَ: until he recovers and becomes well
key_terms.قُرُوحٌ: sores or wounds on the body
key_terms.لَا تَنْكَئُوهَا: do not reopen or aggravate the wounds

ai.seo_question: Should a hadd punishment be delayed if the offender is severely ill or covered with sores?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a legal punishment should be delayed if carrying it out immediately would likely destroy the offender because of severe bodily illness. It reflects the principle that the hadd is not to be administered in a way that causes unlawful killing beyond the prescribed punishment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5030 - In the narration of Al-Sakuni:

It is reported that Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) was brought a man who had committed an offense deserving of a legal punishment (hadd), and the man had numerous sores on his body.
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said: "Delay the execution of the punishment until he recovers. Do not aggravate his sores, lest you kill him."
